decision_conditions: This consent is valid for two years.Reason: In order that the nature of work pertaining to this consent remains appropriate.

Tree work should not be carried out during periods that are likely to interfere with or disturb breeding birds or mammals.Reason: In order to comply with the requirements of the Wildlife and Countryside Act (1981) and Conservation of Habitats and Species Regulations (2010).

a. Prior to the works hereby permitted commencing on site, full details and specification for a proposal to provide and plant one tree (minimum 10-12cm 'Selected Standard' size) to replace that to be removed by virtue of this consent, shall be submitted in writing to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The specification shall include, but not be limited to, the following: the location of the proposed replacement tree; the species of tree and the size (as specified above); the planting methodology; the intended support system; and an aftercare plan.b. All trees included in the specification shall be supplied and planted in accordance with BS 3936-1: 1992 Nursery Stock - Specification for trees and shrubs (or an equivalent British Standard if replaced), BS 8545: 2014 Trees from nursery to independence in the landscape - Recommendations, and the National Plant Specification.c. The planting proposal as detailed in the approved specification must be undertaken at the site in the first planting season [November to March] or part thereof following the commencement of works on site.d. If within a period of five years from the date of planting, the replacement tree, (or if within a period of five years from the date of further planting any tree planted in replacement for it), is removed, uprooted, destroyed or dies, or becomes in the opinion of the local planning authority, seriously damaged or defective, a tree of the same species and size as that originally planted shall be planted in the same place, unless the local planning authority gives its written approval to any variation. The provisions for re-planting as set out in The Town and Country Planning Act 1990 Section 206 continue to apply after the expiration of the five year period hereby stated.Reason: In the interests of visual amenity and in order to maintain tree population at this site after the removal of the preserved tree and in accordance with the requirements of Section 206 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.
